text: Designing good APIs is essential for developers who build applications that talk to each other. One popular approach is REST, which uses simple URLs, called endpoints, to access resources. For example, a user might get data from `/users` or create a new item with `/orders`. A well-designed API must return clear status codes, like `200` for success or `404` if something is not found, so clients know what happened. Also, great documentation is crucial—it helps other developers understand how to use the API without guessing. Finally, versioning (like adding `/v1/` to the URL) ensures that changes don’t break existing users, allowing your API to grow safely over time.
